article.summary: The DNA tests will be conducted at the forensic science laboratories in the Chennai, Madurai and Thanjavur regions.

article.title: Nepal: How are the hundreds of victims from the floods being identified?
article.summary: #Nepal faces a major challenge: identifying the remains that have been found after the #flood that tore through part of the country on August 26, some of which are in an advanced state of decomposition. For #health reasons, the unidentified bodies have begun to be buried. Before each #burial, #DNA samples are taken and an identification number is assigned to each set of remains. Relatives of those reported missing can visit DNA collection centres to provide a sample. Their genetic profile can then be compared with that of the bodies found, in the hope of identifying them. FRANCE 24’s correspondents visited one such centre, set up within the #police #hospital in #Kathmandu.

article.title: Bengal collects blood samples from relatives of people missing in Nepal flood
article.summary: West Bengal is collecting blood samples from relatives of 37 people missing after the August 26 Nepal flash flood for DNA matching.

article.title: After Nepal’s devastating floods, DNA tests help identify victims
article.summary: The recent flash floods in Nepal have left authorities facing a major challenge: identifying the remains that have been recovered, some of which are in an advanced state of decomposition. For health reasons, unidentified bodies have begun to be buried. Before each burial, DNA samples are taken, while relatives of people reported missing can visit DNA collection centres to provide samples of their own. Their genetic profiles can then be compared with those of the recovered remains, in the hope of identifying them. FRANCE 24’s team on the ground reports.

article.title: Nepal floods: Centre to offer DNA profiling services for first-degree relatives of missing persons
article.summary: New Delhi, Sep 04:To facilitate the identification of mortal remains of Nepal flood victims, the Centre will make available the services of central and state-level forensic labs for DNA profiling of their first-degree biological relatives in India, the MEA has said.First-degree biological relatives residing in India -- father, mother, son, daughter or sibling -- may have their biological samples collected and DNA profiles prepared at Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs); State Forensic Science Laboratories (SFSLs); laboratories of the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU); and NABL-accredited laboratories having DNA profiling capability, the ministry said in a statement.The death toll from last week's flash floods in Nepal has risen to at least 1,259 after rescue workers recovered more bodies from affected areas, according to Nepalese authorities.While emergency teams have rescued more than 12,000 people, roughly 5,000 remain missing as search and rescue operations c...
